== Biography ==
Samuel Glasgow lived in West Fallowfield, Chester County, Pennsylvania. His reported birth in 1761 in Pennsylvania remains unverified. He has been placed in the family of [[Glasgow-2870|John Glasgow]] and [[Cranmer-656|Mary Cranmer]], but no inspected Bible entry names him as their son. A different Irish family is now the preferred paternal hypothesis, discussed below.

=== Family and property ===
The memorial associated with Samuel lists Judith as his first wife and Tabitha Wallace Stewart as a later wife, with a reported marriage in 1823. It also lists daughter Margaret Ellen. The dates attached by contributors are Judith 1767–1812, Tabitha 1791–1871 and Margaret Ellen 1824–1829; these are leads, not independently established vital dates.<ref name="SamuelMemorial">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/75056130/samuel_glasgow Find a Grave, memorial 75056130, Samuel Glasgow], contributor family links and stone photograph; current page reviewed 24 October 2026. Theresa Ely photograph added 11 July 2019, file 75056130_4fda28f9-22a7-44f2-9685-4b61ee7bd0eb.jpeg, 370×603. Samuel’s name and 17 May 1824 are legible; the age was not securely read and the photograph supplies no John father clause.</ref>

The Chester deed index associates Samuel with West Fallowfield. Purchases are indexed from John Sweeny in 1804, A3:435, and William Haslett in 1805, A3:433. Sale entries list Judith Heslett in the spouse column, with Abraham Rackstraw in 1805, Y2:391, and James Haslett in 1812, K3:394. The actual deeds have not been read; that indexed form does not establish Judith’s maiden name or kinship with the Hasletts.<ref name="ChesterIndex">Chester County Archives, [https://www.chesco.org/DocumentCenter/View/84215/E-G#page=940 grantor/grantee index, E–G, PDF p.940], Samuel Glasgow entries, visually read 24 October 2026. Index only; deed books A3:433, A3:435, Y2:391 and K3:394 remain uninspected.</ref>

=== Will and death ===
Samuel’s will, dated 17 May 1824 and proved 31 May 1824, names wife Tabitha and infant daughter Margaret Ellen. A contingent remainder goes to the sons of his three brothers William, James and Robert Glasgow in Ireland. The brothers are not the testator’s sons; their sons are the beneficiaries.<ref name="ChesterWill">Chester County, estate 7520, Samuel Glasgow of West Fallowfield, will 17 May 1824, proved 31 May 1824, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 original will, portal pp.588–589], scanned volume 07451–7600. Estate cover p.586. Original visually read 23 October 2026.</ref>

Robert Futhey and Thomas Stewart were appointed executors; office alone does not prove kinship. Samuel Glasgow Haslett is described as James Haslett’s infant twin son, not as the testator’s son; no godparent relationship is stated. Later accounts name Benjamin Glasgow as a debtor and William Glasgow in transmitting a legacy from another estate, without specifying their relationship to Samuel.<ref name="ChesterAccounts">Chester County estate 7520, portal Doc773006, pp.594 and 596, later estate accounts; [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=594&repo=r-24f48cc6 original accounts].</ref>

The combination of Tabitha, infant Margaret Ellen, Judith and the West Fallowfield property trail identifies Samuel with this estate at 98%. His memorial stone bears 17 May 1824, also the will date; the stone does not securely establish his age. No new birth or death correction is inferred from the contributor family display.<ref name="SamuelMemorial" /><ref name="ChesterWill" /><ref name="ChesterIndex" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Preferred Irish father and competing John family ===
[[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] is the preferred identification of Samuel’s father, assessed '''67% probable'''. The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris names James and [[Rutherford-4861|Margaret Rutherford]]’s sons William, Robert, James near Moneymore and Samuel who went to America, together with daughter Ellen. The will’s three Irish brothers supply a specific matching family configuration. The letter does not name the Chester testator, and the will names no father: the conclusion is an inference from their combined evidence, not an explicit parent clause.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio(1990), printed pp.8–12; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-J pp.8–9], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], DGS007834162, images1564–1566. PRONI T1959 anonymous family recollection, in [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Albert Rutherford’s reproduction]; original letter uninspected. Chester County estate7520, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 original will, pp588–589], previously inspected23October2026.</ref>

[[Glasgow-2870|John Glasgow]] remains an unselected alternative at '''25% uncertain''', reduced from the earlier 72% probable assessment. The John/Mary Cranmer reconstruction and Samuel’s reported 1761 Pennsylvania birth remain substantive competing claims. John’s Bible narrative concerns Mary and son John’s burials and Bible transmission, without an inspected literal Samuel entry. The stone does not name John as father. The earlier 72% assessment relied on regional generation, burial and the Bible locator, which cannot outweigh the specific Irish brother configuration without checking the actual Bible.

The proposed Irish family has serious unresolved chronology. If Samuel’s 1761 birth and James-1025’s alleged 1759 death are established, they could defeat this paternal identification. Margaret Rutherford’s estimated birth about 1700 also requires testing. Neither the maternal attachment nor any life date is changed to fit the hypothesis. [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel Glasgow]]’s estimated 1726 birth must not be transferred to this Chester man: the identities remain unresolved and no merge follows.

The full-letter tradition was read on 20 October 2026; Faris’s printed pp.8–12 subsequently confirmed its structure. Faris and Albert Rutherford reproduce a dependent anonymous family recollection, not independent witnesses. Faris calls it file5 within PRONI T1959, whereas the reproduced transcription cites T1959/3; the discrepancy and original letter remain unchecked. The 1759 probate index gives Drumcarn but no kin, so it has not identified the older James. William is called eldest in the letter although the imported birth estimates put him later. Faris also notes the tension between Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in 1824 and the proposed early paternal death. These are open identity questions.

The four Irish family father assessments remain James-1024 78%, Samuel-1492 76%, Robert-2425 77% and William-2426 84%, all probable, for the James/Margaret family roles. They do not strengthen the American Robert-12, Arthur-649 and Joseph-1543 father links, each 35%, John-4027 at 30%, or Mary-4030 at 22%. James-1025’s own father William-1026 remains 32%. No Scottish migration or new maternal identification is established.

=== Other Samuel and Missouri comparisons ===
[[Glasgow-3823|Samuel Glasgow]], the younger East Nottingham man whose records concern a Free People of Color family and emigration to Liberia, remains a separate unadopted comparison. Name and neighbouring townships do not establish a parent relationship; community classification is not a biological exclusion. No son or mother is assigned from that comparison.

[[Glasgow-45|James Glasgow]], the probable Downington-born drummer, is absent from the inspected will and later accounts. That absence does not exclude a son, but neither this estate nor the military entry selects a named father. The immigrant-father and Philadelphia-estate tradition remains unproved.

=== Further evidence ===
The actual deeds, a literal Samuel entry in the family Bible and independent evidence for the 1761 Pennsylvania birth and the older James’s alleged 1759 death are the main discriminators. The original Chester Samuel will has been inspected. Its identification with the letter-defined Samuel-1492 remains unresolved; the original family letter and deeds remain uninspected. No change of life dates, maternal grades or live WikiTree family fields is implied.
